body:
Hi, this is looking very good!
I'm personally in favour of this change. When dealing with `Packed*Arrays` I found them to be a bit lacking in terms of exposed functionality. This is a welcome addition in my mind!

The implementation looks pretty optimal to me, and I think it feels right at home in `Span`.

However, I'm trying to establish `Span` to be unopinionated in another PR (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104286). 
If that gets merged, it would mean that negative or out-of-bounds index checks should be performed outside of `Span`, in the user facing functions (causing some duplicate code in `Vector` and `String` separately). My reasoning for this is because opinionated code should be explicit.
The other PR is accepted for a merge, so unless someone has concerns, we shouldn't have to wait long for that :)

The name `find_seq` and documentation work for me.

Looking at this again, I'm very happy with the decision to have the containers do the logic and `Span` do the dumb but fast implementation. This feels sane to me.

I'd like to ask you to harmonize the two functions though, according to adjustments made in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104286/ regarding boundary conditions. In particular:
- Negative indices from `-1` to `-size() -1` are indices starting from the back
- Negative indices beyond that and indices above `size()` are incorrect indices and return -1

This will change behavior in the `String` implementation, but I think it's worth it for consistency in the long run.

Awesome, it's looking perfect now! Thanks for indulging all my feedback :)

Just needs a rebase onto `master` because my other PR got merged.
Also, you'll need to re-run `doctool` because the `default` values in the `xml` are out of sync (still 0 for `rfind_seq` instead of `-1`).

Finally, I think it would be good to hear one or two more voices on whether we should add / expose this feature in the first place. I personally think so, but I'm not the only or most relevant voice for this :)

Just bringing a quick update: We've found a problem with negative indexes, and were trying to figure out together on chat how best to handle this.

I'll summarize it quickly here:
```
# What should this do?
"ABCDEF".rfind_seq("CD", -2)
```

We see 3 options:
- Old behavior: recognize as "invalid index" and default to normal search, i.e. iterate from index `4 to 0`
- Interpret `-2` as an index into the array, but clamp to a valid search index, i.e. iterate from `4 to 0`
- Interpret `-2` as an index into the search space, i.e. iterate from `3 to 0`

Personally, I think the correct choice would be to use the third option. It's consistent with forwards and backwards iterating logic, basically using back anchors for back indexes and front anchors for forward indexes. The search space is the following:

```
CD
ABCDEF

 CD
ABCDEF

  CD
ABCDEF

   CD
ABCDEF

    CD
ABCDEF
```

A value of `-1` can be interpreted as "start from the back", while `-2` can be interpreted as "start from the back, but skip one index", etc.

I can see that it's a bit confusing, but it generalizes to size 1 behavior, and is consistent with theoretical equal slicing behavior:
```
# -0 indexing does not exist, but hopefully you get the gist:
"ABCDEF"[:].rfind_seq("ABC") == "ABCDEF".rfind_seq("ABC", -1)
"ABCDEF"[:-1].rfind_seq("ABC") == "ABCDEF".rfind_seq("ABC", -2)
"ABCDEF"[:-2].rfind_seq("ABC") == "ABCDEF".rfind_seq("ABC", -3)
# [...]
```

It would be interesting to hear more opinions on this. It's certainly not a trivial problem!
But I think we should probably not merge this until we can settle on a behavior.

Hi! Sorry for getting back to you so late. This is a hard decision to make indeed!

I finally got around to thinking about this again, but I reached the same conclusion as I did earlier - the only 'consistent' behavior would be to make `-1` the "last possible index in the search space". Making it the last index in the 'search string' would require more complex logic, for questionable benefit. I really tried to like your suggestion, but it doesn't work for me. I hope that's ok!

Let try to get this merged (or at least mergable, someone may still object to this being added) in time for 4.5 :)

I think there's still a hole in the logic; a few small changes should fix this.

Just one more thing, should probably keep caching `length()` values for inner loops.

Otherwise, it's perfect now, in my opinion! Thanks for all the hard work.

We'll probably need at least one more opinion before we merge this.
In particular, it's interesting to know:

- Whether we want to expose this function (see https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11722).
- Whether we're ready to change all `find` functions' negative indexing (from "fail and / or lax" to consistent negative indexing behavior).
- Whether the wording in the docs is appropriate.

I'd like to point out that we discussed this change in the core meeting, and while it seemed the feature may be useful, there were no other opinions on implementation details.

Looks great to me! Thank you again for going through all these iterations.
We're past the 4.5 feature freeze now, so let's aim for 4.6 dev 1 to merge this. It would be nice to get final docs feedback on the `.xml` changes too.
